lines: First stop:
a company the coffee shop pays to handle its cards.
It works for the shop, not for ZERO.
And it has no idea who he is.
It only reads the first digits of the card number.
They say which network to ask,
and which bank is behind the card.
Which raises a better question.
Why does a coffee need a network at all?
Because thousands of banks issue cards,
and millions of shops take them.
Most of them have never met.
The network is where they all agree to meet,
under one set of rules.
In the U.S., that's mostly Visa or Mastercard.
In a single year, Visa alone handled 258 billion payments.
That's about eight thousand every second.
All of it runs through four giant data centers,
with spare power,
spare cooling
and spare connections,
so a question never has to wait.
Here's the strange part.
The network doesn't move money either.
It moves questions.
Last stop: ZERO's bank.
The one that gave him the card.
It has a fraction of a second to answer two things.
Does he have enough credit?
And is this really him?
For the second one, it doesn't ask ZERO.
It asks his habits.
Visa says its own system weighs more than five hundred details about every payment,
in about a millisecond.
But ZERO's card is brand new.
He has no habits.
And to a fraud machine,
no history can look a lot like a stolen card.
Back in the coffee shop,
the clock says one point one seconds.
If a bank ever takes too long, or goes down,
the network can answer for it,
using AI to stand in.
But ZERO's bank isn't down.
It's just not sure.
Then the evidence adds up.
A real chip,
one only the real card can make.
A tiny amount.
A coffee shop a few blocks from his address.
Credit: yes.
And now look at what the bank actually does.
It doesn't send any money.
It puts a hold on four seventy-five of ZERO's credit line.
A promise.
And the promise works both ways.
If the coffee never showed up,
ZERO could dispute the charge,
and the money would be pulled back from the shop.
The answer rides back the same way.
Bank,
network,
the shop's company,
the terminal.
Two seconds.
ZERO thinks he just paid.
He didn't.
Nobody has paid anybody.
Not yet.
So when does the money actually move?
